question: It was determined that a total-flooding carbon dioxide suppression system installed in a process room requires an overpressurization vent. The system will flow 156 pounds of carbon dioxide per minute, and the enclosure strength has been calculated to be 9 lb/ft2 (71 kg). What is the minimum vent size recommended for this application? A. 35 in2 (226 cm2) B. 40 in2 (258 cm2) C. 45 in2 (290 cm2) D. 50 in2 (323 cm2)

How much depth of particle-sized dusts of organic materials such as wood or food products can, under the right set of conditions, result in a flash fire or explosion? A. Less than 1/8 in. (3 mm) B. Between 1/8 and 1/4 in. (3 mm to 6.4 mm) C. Between 1/4 and 1/2 in. (6.4 mm to 12.7 mm) D. At least 1/2 in. (12.7 mm)

The performance of fire alarm audible notification in a wide open space can be analyzed using a condition called free-field condition, where the sound pressure level (SPL) decreases roughly by a specific decibel value every time the distance from the source is doubled. Which of the following choices is the specific decibel value attributed to the free-field condition? A. 1 dB B. 3 dB C. 5 dB D. 6 dB
When vaporization of a solid occurs with chemical decomposition, it is known as: A. melting. B. sublimation. C. evaporation. D. pyrolysis.
Electrical equipment used in Class I, Division I hazardous locations is often referred to as: A. intrinsically safe B. explosion resistant. C. propagation resistant. D. explosion proof.

The entrainment of air from the surrounding atmosphere in a rising fire plume has the effect of: A. decreasing the total mass/volume of the plume, cooling the plume, concentrating the fire products. B. increasing the total mass/volume of the plume, heating the plume, reducing the concentration of fire products. C. decreasing the total mass/volume of the plume, heating the plume diluting the concentration of fire products. D. increasing the total mass/volume of the plume, cooling the plume, diluting the concentration of fire products.

During which stage of a fire would the heat release likely to be controlled by the fuel package size and geometry (i.e. the surface area likely to burn)? A. Incipient Stage B. Growth Stage C. Steady-state Stage D. Decay Stage
Which of the following materials is considered by NFPA to be a Group A plastic? A. Butyl rubber B. Natural rubber (not expanded) C. Silicone rubber D. Cloroprene rubber
Which of the following refrigerants has the highest flammability, according to its Safety Group classification? A. Octaflouropropane B. Difluoromethane C. Methyl Chloride D. Methane

In assessing the use of a sprinkler head with a Nominal K-Factor of 14.0, you find that this sprinkler head provides what percentage of the flow from a Nominal K-Factor 5.6 sprinkler device? A. 100% B. 140% C. 250% D. 300%

The driving force behind every inspection, testing, and maintenance program for fire alarm systems is to: A. develop a Record of Inspections. B. make system reliability as high as possible. C. identify deficiencies for corrective action. D. comply with Authority Having Jurisdiction requirements.

In a building structure, components like shear walls, braced frames, and moment-resisting frames, as well as foundations and diaphragms form the basis for what type of structural system? A. Vertical Support System B. Lateral Force-Resisting System C. Longitudinal System D. Foundation System

An IT server room housing sensitive electronic equipment requires a fire suppression system. The room has air-conditioning and power systems that may have hot surfaces, is fitted with an over-pressure relief system and may occasionally be occupied by workers. Which would be the preferred gaseous fire extinguishing agent? A. Halocarbon Clean Agent B. Inert Clean Agent C. Carbon Dioxide D. Halon 1301

Most model Building Codes address fire spread due to radiant heat ignition of adjacent building facades by specifying a minimum set back from the property line determined using a piloted ignition heat flux similar to that of: A. exterior wood cladding. B. horizontal vinyl siding. C. masonry brick façade. D. horizontal aluminum siding.

To which of the following fires would infrared flame detectors be non-responsive? A. Ethylene and propylene oxide fires B. Gasoline and diesel fuel fires C. Jet fuel and butane fires D. Sulfur and hydrogen fires

In order to meet the NEC (NFPA 70) requirements for emergency service, how long must the on-site fuel supply be able to operate the prime mover at full engine-generator output? A. 1 Hour B. 1.5 Hours C. 2 Hours D. 3 Hours

Piloted ignition temperatures of solids are influenced by: A. air movement, rate of heating, size and shape of fuel load. B. ambient air temperature, conductivity, and height of fuel load. C. air pressure, reactivity, and width of fuel load. D. composition, chemical changes, and size of fuel load.
Design calculations are specified in the building codes. Those calculations contain special reduction factors and are identified by the following value: A. O B. P C. Q D. R
A municipality which anticipates a maximum demand of 5000 gpm (18,925 lpm) during a large fire should be capable of providing such flow for a duration of: A. 4 hours B. 5 hours C. 6 hours D. 8 hours
Type II 222 construction would require exterior bearing walls supporting only 1 floor to have a fire resistance rating of: A. 1 hour B. 2 hours C. 3 hours D. 4 hours

When applying rate-of-rise heat detectors, use care to avoid locating them in areas where temperatures might normally be expected to rise as much as ____________ in 1 minute (or less) in order to avoid unwanted alarms. A. 10 to 15°F (5.6 - 8.4°C) B. 12 to 15°F (6.7 - 8.4°C) C. 12 to 20°F (6.7 - 11.2°C) D. 15 to 20°F (8.4 - 11.2°C)

At a temperature of 0°F (-18° C) the heat loss from an elevated steel tank with a capacity of 100,000 gal (378 M3) is equal to: A. 352 Btu/hr (103 W) B. 367 Btu/hr (108 W) C. 423 Btu/hr (124 W) D. 480 Btu/hr (141 W)

While many detection systems are available, heat detection is the basis of sprinkler system response. In terms of sprinkler systems, what type of heat release is most associated with their activation? A. conduction B. endothermic C. convection D. radiation

Idle wood pallets are stored outside (not sprinklered) in piles of 100 pallets each. What is the minimum recommended clearance between the pallet piles and a metal building? A. 10 ft (3.0 m) B. 20 ft (6.1 m) C. 30 ft (9.1 m) D. 50 ft (15.2 m)

What is the minimum safe distance combustibles should be moved from the work areas when performing welding, cutting or other hot work? A. 25 feet (7.6 meters) B. 30 feet (9.1 meters) C. 35 feet (10.6 meters) D. 40 feet (12.1 meters)

When constructing the foundation for a tank or tower installation, the compressive strength of the concrete should be not less than: A. 1,000 psi (6.89 MPa) B. 2,000 psi (13.79 MPa) C. 3,000 psi (20.69 MPa) D. 4,000 psi (27.59 MPa)
The NFPA document Standard On Operations and Training for Technical Search and Rescue Incidents is known as: A. NFPA 1670 B. NFPA 1600 C. NFPA 1006 D. NFPA 1076

CASE STUDY: You are a claims adjuster working for an insurance company. You received notice of a fire event at an industrial facility. You are now charged with conducting a fire investigation to evaluate the merits of the claim. Please answer the following three questions regarding the fire investigation. Which of the following will ensure you are conducting a legally valid scene investigation? A. Permission from the owner B. Fire chief approval C. Approval from your employer D. No approval is needed

There are two different ambient noise levels that are required to meet fire alarm audibility goals and system design. The first is the average sound pressure levels (SPL) during the time the area is occupied. The second is the maximum SPL that lasts a specific minimum duration of time (in seconds). Per NFPA 72, which of the following choices is the minimum duration required to meet the second ambient noise level? A. 30 seconds B. 60 seconds C. 120 seconds D. 160 seconds

While performing a fire hazard survey on a structure in a non-hydrant area you need to estimate the water supply capacity of a stream adjacent to the structure as a possible drafting site. The stream is 5' wide and the average depth is 12". You observe that a leaf floating on the surface travels 10 feet in 30 seconds from the current. What is the approximate flow rate in gallons per minute (GPM) of the stream? A. 250 GPM (946 LPM) B. 500 GPM (1,892 LPM) C. 750 GPM (2,839 LPM) D. 1,000 GPM (3,785 LPM)

Panic hardware that has been tested and listed for use on fire protection-rated doors is designed to release the latching device at a pressure not to exceed _______? A. 5 lbs (2.3 kg) B. 10 lbs (4.5 kg) C. 15 lbs (6.8 kg) D. 20 lbs (9.1 kg)

In oil and chemical plants, what is the minimum interunit spacing between high-hazard process units, according to recommendations developed by GE Global Asset Protection Services? A. 100 feet (30.5 meters) B. 200 feet (61 meters) C. 300 feet (91.5 meters) D. 400 feet (122 meters)
What is the fire resistance rating for a Type I 442 exterior wall supporting more than one floor or column or other load bearing wall? A. 1 hour B. 2 hours C. 3 hours D. 4 hours

When constructing a ground level water tank, the four seismic considerations are: A. Anchorage of the tank and foundation, clearance around the pipe penetrations through the pump house or other structural walls, proper steel thickness near base of the tank and flexibility of pipe connections to the tank. B. Flexibility of pipe connections at the pump, a proper foundation, protected pipe penetrations and reinforced walls. C. Design by a qualified structural engineer, use of appropriate steel of appropriate thickness, flexible pipe connections throughout, anchorage to a concrete base. D. Welded solid steel connections to the tank base, anchorage of the tank and foundation, clearance around pipe penetrations, and consideration of expected wind loads.

Limited combustible building construction materials have a potential heat value not exceeding what value? A. 3,000 BTU/LB (6.98 kj/gr) B. 3,500 BTU/LB (8.14 kj/gr) C. 4,000 BTU/LB (9.30 kj/gr) D. 4,500 BTU/LB (10.47 kj/gr)

Fire burns in three dimensional space, with flames attaching to inclined surfaces leading to a number of observed behaviors. Flames from a fire burning in a channel inclined at 10° above the horizontal will behave in a manner similar to: A. A pool fire B. A trench fire C. A wall fire D. A ceiling fire

When calculating friction loss in a sprinkler system, it is generally accepted that a 90° standard elbow of 2 in. (50 mm) in diameter is the equivalent of: A. 2 feet of pipe (0.6 m) B. 3 feet of pipe (0.9 m) C. 5 feet of pipe (1.5m) D. 6 feet of pipe (1.8 m)

Enclosed fires are generally considered to have four distinct phases. What are they? A. Incipient, growth, fully developed, decay B. Ignition, smoldering, free burning, ash C. Incipient, developing, developed, decay D. Pyrolytic, growing, fully developed, decaying

Vortex shedding involves interactions between: A. diameter of the pool, material burning, and radiant emissions. B. air flow, emissive heat release, and the width of the pool. C. inflowing air, material burning, and the pool boundary D. inflowing air, the fire plume, and the pool boundary

Following several hotel fires, several studies were conducted to ascertain the most frequent first action taken by hotel guests in the event of a fire. These studies discovered a phenomenon known as a convergence cluster. What is considered to be a positive indication of an occurrence of a convergence cluster? A. Progression to evacuation B. Attempted evacuation C. Offered refuge in room D. Awareness of fire incident

The four operating principles of automatic sprinklers demand that they be: A. mechanically simple, require little maintenance, be reliable in operation, and free from premature operation B. rugged, mechanically simple, reliable in operation, and free from premature operation C. reliable in operation, free from premature operation, capable of operation in a multitude of environments, and capable of extinguishing the involved materials D. mechanically simple, rugged, require little maintenance, and free from premature operation

Boyce, Shields, and Silcock study on reading exit signs resulted in which type of sign as the most visible to impaired persons? A. Color contrasted sign B. Non-illuminated exit sign C. Illuminated exit sign D. Light emitting diode (LED) sign

You are evaluating the storage arrangement to determine appropriate sprinkler system protection requirements. Which of the following is an important consideration when determining sprinkler system design requirements? A. Building construction B. Storage height C. Type and number of fire alarms D. Indoor Hose Connections
Fire protection design for IT rooms must take into account that damage to magnetic media begins above what temperature? A. 125°F (52°C) B. 150°F (66°C) C. 174°F (79°C) D. 350°F (176°C)
The sources of pressure head commonly found in fire protection hydraulic systems includes gravity, pumping, pneumatic, and: A. static. B. vacuum. C. combination. D. dynamic.

While temperature is often referenced when speaking of fire and its consequences, the underlying process of heat transfer can be said to govern fire: A. from pyrolysis through to ash. B. from ignition, through fully developed, to structural failure. C. from incipient stage through to fully developed. D. from pre-ignition through to free burning.

At how many years old shall fixed temperature nonrestorable heat detectors be tested, at which time they are either replaced or a sample is removed and tested for continual operability? A. 5 Years B. 10 Years C. 15 Years D. 20 Years
According to NFPA 220, Type V indicates what type of building construction? A. Fire Resistive B. Ordinary C. Wood Frame D. Non Combustible
Upward flame spread is also known as what? A. Combustible flame spread B. Concurrent flow flame spread C. Ceiling plume flame spread D. Ceiling radiant flame spread
The two important characteristics for a fire department pumper are: A. the net RPM and pressure B. the net volume and pressure C. the discharge RPM and pressure. D. the discharge volume and pressure

Community risk management is a requirement of NFPA 1500 and can be systematically looked at through the Risk Management Model, which requires: A. identifying risk, evaluating risk, establishing priorities, establishing control techniques, and monitoring. B. assessing building stock, setting priorities for response, assignment of appropriate equipment, delineating command, and control. C. identifying risk factors, proposing mitigation strategies, implementing developed programs, and monitoring for compliance. D. evaluating current emergency management process, assessing municipal building design factors, establishing priorities, and designing program parameters.
What flowing pressure of a sprinkler is generally considered a minimum for development of a reasonable spray pattern? A. 5 PSI (34 KPA) B. 7 PSI (48 KPA) C. 10 PSI (69 KPA) D. 14 PSI (97 KPA)
What percentage of the Insurance Services Office Fire Suppression Rating Schedule is based on the city’s water supply? A. 20% B. 30% C. 40% D. 50%

Which of the following types of smoke detectors offer advantages in large open areas such as aircraft hangers? A. Ionization smoke detectors B. Photoelectric smoke detectors C. Air sampling-type smoke detectors D. Video-based smoke detectors

In order to qualify as a "PUMPER" under NFPA 1901, a fire department vehicle must be capable of pumping at least: A. 250 GPM (950 L/min). B. 750 GPM (2,850 L/min). C. 1,250 GPM (4,700 L/min). D. 3,000 GPM (11,356 L/min).

What Class would a duct material meet with a flame spread rating of 20, an inside surface smoke development rating of 30, and an outside surface smoke development rating of 45? A. Class 0 B. Class 1 C. Class 2 D. Class 2C

A waste material with which of the following characteristics is considered a hazardous waste under the United States Federal Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA)? A. PH ≤ 2 or ≥ 12.5, or a liquid flashpoint of 140°F (60°C) or less B. PH ≤ 2 or ≥ 12.5, or a liquid flashpoint of 100°F (37.7°C) or less C. PH ≥ 7 or ≤ 11, or a liquid flashpoint of 140°F (60°C) or less D. PH ≥12.5, or a liquid flashpoint of 200°F (93.3°C) or less

Microbiologicaily Influenced Corrosion (MIC) can manifest as several forms of corrosion, including: A. pitting, crevice, cratering, and filiform B. uniform, chemical, stray current, and general carburization C. high temperature, galvanic, pitting, and chemical D. dealloying, filiform, molten salt, and galvanic

The nature of the mechanical systems is to use networks of pipes and ducts to connect various parts of the building. Even when the systems are off, these networks can provide routes through the building that allow the spread of fire, smoke, and biological or chemical compounds, causing the danger to spread beyond the hazard's origin. Which of the following is considered to be a building design element that can limit the likelihood of such a system from spreading fire, smoke or chemicals through a building? A. Open-loop systems B. Automatic dampers C. Common duct networks D. Defensible space

A loss control consultant at XYZ Insurance Company must conduct an onsite risk assessment at an insured storage facility. In one portion of the facility, there is bulk storage of aerosols. What NFPA standard must the consultant reference for fire protection requirements? A. NFPA 13 B. NFPA 30 C. NFPA 30B D. NFPA 72
When doing an event-tree analysis, what is the term for an event with the likelihood of occurring several times during a system's life (p>0 001)? A. Frequent B. Probable C. Remote D. Improbable
